label: The problem
show: Five dots, one turns amber. A bar: 4 in 10 get treatment. Then thin lines that slip down over weeks and fade.
text: One in five American teenagers goes through depression in a year, and most get no treatment. It builds slowly: a little less sleep, fewer texts, dropped plans. Nobody knows when to ask.

label: What we built
show: The Stability mark draws itself. Two phones slide in: Maya's and her mom's.
text: That's why we built Stability. It lives on a teenager's phone, linked to a parent's. Meet Maya.

label: Her whole digital life
show: Maya's phone in the centre. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, browsing and news feeds light up on the left; Spotify, games and chats on the right, under '17 sources'. Then Stable floats in, drifts around, and settles into the check-in card on her phone.
text: Stability connects to her whole digital life: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, browsing, news feeds, Spotify, games and chats. It reads it all on her phone and learns her normal. Once a week, our mascot, Stable, checks in. Two taps.

label: It asks
show: Week four: the two questions come up and she answers low. Weeks five and six: the ring turns amber, her check-ins climb, the model's score crosses its line, and the questions come up again.
text: Every month, it asks the two questions doctors use. Maya says she's mostly okay, and it takes her at her word. Then finals hit. Her check-ins get tense, and our model doesn't wait a month. It asks again.

label: The note
show: Week six she answers low again. Week eight her answers are high. Mom's phone slides in. An amber dot crosses from Maya's phone to hers and the note opens.
text: But at week eight, her answers come back high. Maya sees a nudge to see a doctor, and her mom gets a note: what changed, for how long, and how to start the conversation. Never her messages.

label: Private, with a safety net
show: Maya types a message. It becomes a bubble, then a single dot. A counter holds at 0 bytes sent. A chip: 988, one tap away.
text: Nothing she types, watches or searches ever leaves her phone. Small models read it there and keep only numbers. If she types or searches for self-harm, 988 is one tap away.

label: The engine
show: A diagram builds: her digital life, two taps and past answers feed the engine; it opens the two questions, then the eight, then the note. Below, the two on-phone models and a lock: 0 words leave the phone.
text: Under the hood, her digital life, Stable's two taps and her past answers feed our engine. It tracks how she's doing and decides when to ask. High answers unlock the full eight questions, and only then is a parent told.

label: It works
show: A counter runs to 400,000+. Tiles: 3.4x (the ask model 44% vs a fixed schedule 13%), 0.90 on 113 teens, 54% vs 24% (US high schoolers sleeping 4 hours or less vs 8 hours who felt sad or hopeless), and 2x with 13 of 15.
text: And it works. Tested on over four hundred thousand real examples, our ask model finds a hard week three times as often as a schedule, and scored point nine oh on a hundred thirteen teens it had never seen. Across thirty thousand US high schoolers, those sleeping four hours or less were twice as likely to feel sad or hopeless. Our language models catch twice what keyword lists do.

label: Close
show: The Stability mark, 'knowing when to ask', and a small 'Prototype. Not medical advice.'
text: Stability. Knowing when to ask, so more teens get help sooner.
